messages:
alex: Heads-up: ran kernel-sampler job on a mixed farm overnight. Found a weird flip at seqlen=256 where the fp8 path picks slower matmul kernels when KV cache hit rate > 60%.
maya: hmm that's new. Did the sampler include hw-fingerprint overrides (driver quirks)?
achlex: (typo) alex: yes — probe included pci_vendor/device + sm version + driver. We still saw kernel choice oscillate between 'tc_gemm_v1' and 'fallback_tile4' after ~1200 tokens.
chris: can you paste the sampler cmd and a short perf snippet?
alex: sure:
```
./kernel-sampler --id farm-3 --model lla-13b --probe-seqlen 64,128,256,512 \
  --repeat 3 --hw-probe=sm,tc,fp8,bf16 --collect=kerneltimes,kv-hits
```
maya: perf summary (aggregate, warm/steady windows):
- seqlen=64: tc_gemm_v1 median 3.8ms
- seqlen=128: tc_gemm_v1 median 6.2ms
- seqlen=256: fallback_tile4 median 14.1ms (tc_gemm_v1 median 18.4ms)
- kv-hit rate at seqlen=256: 62% (steady)
chris: So autotune picked fallback_tile4 for seqlen=256 due to lower variance under high KV pressure?
alex: Exactly. But on a different host with same SM (sm86) and different driver 540.x we got tc_gemm_v1 faster at 256.
maya: suspect driver/runtime interaction + bank-conflicts under high KV-copy. We should capture occupancy + shared mem stall counters.
runtime-bot: Added job: infra/probes/kernel-sampler/1718000000 to perf dashboard. Link: https://perf.internal/reports/1718000000
sre: FYI — this pattern caused a 2.3% tail latency bump on prod pool last night (seqlen distribution shifted toward 256). Investigating autoscaler churn correlation.
chris: Proposal: change autotune heuristic to two-phase sampling: quick warm probes (short bursts) to detect kernel latency floor, then sustained probes under simulated KV-hit pressure to capture stability. Also add driver-version as tie-breaker.
maya: +1. Also add a cheap microbench to detect bf16 path correctness; if bf16 path unstable then prefer fallback even if slightly faster.
alex: I'll prototype change: sample windows = {burst: 20 requests, steady: 200 requests with preloaded KV cache}. Add metrics: p50/p95/stddev and kernel-switch count.
chris: incremental rollout: canary on Dedicated pool A, observe 24h. If tail latency drops, roll to other pools.
maya: small note — update the model profile to record 'preferred_kernel_by_seqlen' and 'preferred_kernel_when_kv>50%'. That'll help routing.
alex: doing that. Will post results tomorrow. :coffee:
